items.title: 32.8 Effect of Climate Change on Crops

blocks.text: Agriculture is the industry most vulnerable to a changing climate. Changes in temperature, rainfall and extreme weather caused by climate change directly affect farming. Heat causes dehydration, which leads to poor photosynthesis and respiration. Higher temperatures can speed up a plant's metabolism, but if plants get too hot they suffer heat stress, which reduces growth and yield. Cold weather also damages some crops and can kill young plants, causing complete loss of yield.

items: Rainfall: normal rain gives plants the water and nutrients they need, but changing rainfall patterns can cause drought in some areas and floods in others, both of which can make crops fail; unpredictable rain and cloudbursts erode the nutrient-rich topsoil.

Extreme events: hurricanes, heatwaves and hailstorms can destroy crops and farm infrastructure, leading to food shortages. Storms uproot plants and break branches, strong winds cause water loss and drought, and hail damages leaves, fruit and stems; severe hail can destroy the whole crop.
Heat and UV: a higher UV index and heatwaves put crops under severe heat stress, speeding up water loss and possibly burning leaves.

blocks.text: To adapt to these changes, scientists are developing crop varieties that are more resilient to different climates, such as drought-resistant maize and heat-tolerant wheat. Drought-tolerant and flood-proof traits have also been developed; for example, 'Sub1 rice' can survive being submerged under water for two weeks.

blocks.prompt: Give two ways in which climate change can reduce crop yields.
blocks.explanation: Any two of: heat stress and dehydration; drought or floods from changed rainfall; erosion of topsoil by cloudbursts; destruction by storms, hail or heatwaves; frost killing young plants.

items: Heat, cold, drought, floods, storms and hail reduce yields.
New varieties: drought-resistant maize, heat-tolerant wheat, Sub1 rice (survives two weeks under water).
